clue.text: Ancient pile in northern location on 17

parts.note: ancient means old
a cock is a small heap of hay, as in haycock
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of some old building standing somewhere in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is PUB CRAWL, so a location on it is a pub. 'Pile' looks like a grand building but is a heap of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub is a stop on a crawl, and the Old Cock Inn is a typical English pub name.

clue.text: Edges trimmed to instructions

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, so the word for edges loses its opening letter

parts.note: edges are borders

explanation.surface: A gardener told to trim the edges of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: BORDERS loses its first letter, B, to the instruction 'trimmed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orders are commands or instructions given to someone to carry out.

clue.text: 17 leg wound treated with vitamin injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the vitamin letter goes into the rearranged letters
a treated wound has been worked on, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: C is a vitamin

explanation.surface: A leg wound being treated with a vitamin injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' rearranges WOUND to DUNOW, and the 'injection' puts C inside it. 17 is PUB CRAWL, so a leg of it is one pub along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dun Cow is a common pub name, one stop or leg on a pub crawl.

clue.text: Singular offer sourly spelled out — the response to which might be a bitter outpouring

definitions.text: the response to which might be a bitter outpouring

parts.note: singular means one

indicators.note: spelled out here means set out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone making a grudging offer that has to be spelled out, met by a bitter outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelled out' rearranges OFFER SOURLY into the last two words. The definition hides a pint of bitter being poured for the barman.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying the barman a drink with these words may well lead to a bitter being poured, a beer rather than resentment.

clue.text: After end of Woodstock Ringo — Wings having been dropped — and Dead tour stadium where Beatles played part of 17

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the first one in the answer
end of picks out the final letter of Woodstock
wings are the outer letters, so Ringo loses its first and last

parts.note: the Beatles played Shea Stadium in New York in 1965

explanation.surface: Rock history: Woodstock, Ringo, Paul McCartney's Wings and the Grateful Dead touring stadiums.
explanation.walkthrough: K, ING, SHEA and D join up. 'Tour' just joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The King's Head is a familiar pub name, so it can be one part of a pub crawl.

clue.text: Tenor horn's art shown off in 17 venue

indicators.note: shown off suggests letters flung about for display, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: A tenor horn player showing off their artistry at a pub venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown off' rearranges T with HORNSART.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Star is a common pub name, a venue to visit on a pub crawl.

clue.text: See 5
'I Am Satan' remade as 'Devil's Island'

indicators.note: remade means made again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horror film called I Am Satan remade under a new title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil's Island' is also a real French penal colony, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is home to the Tasmanian devil, a marsupial found only there, so it is the devil's island.

clue.text: Abbot is an enigma in black and white likely to make one 23

definitions.text: in black and white likely to make one 23

parts.note: Russ Abbot is a British comedian

indicators.note: an enigma is a puzzle, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about an abbot being a puzzle in black and white habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enigma' is the anagram signal, nodding to Churchill calling Russia an enigma. 23 is SQUIFFY, meaning tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Russian and White Russian are vodka cocktails, likely to leave a drinker tipsy.

clue.text: Cancan on tuba played with unexpected élan to emulate sound of 26

parts.note: a can is a tin, and two of them give two tins

indicators.note: played and unexpected both suggest letters thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the accent

explanation.surface: A band playing a cancan on the tuba with surprising flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played with unexpected' rearranges TUBA ELAN to NABULATE. 26 is NELL, which sounds like knell, the tolling of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To tintinnabulate is to ring like bells, like a funeral knell.

clue.text: 2 swapping sleeveless gown for England top is an idiot

indicators.note: swapping means one piece is exchanged for another

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer to clue 2, the pub name

indicators.note: sleeveless means without the outer letters, so only the middle of gown remains
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone swapping a sleeveless gown for an England shirt is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: In DUN COW, OW from the middle of 'gown' is replaced by E, the first letter of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow learner or fool, so an idiot fits well.

clue.text: Legendary victim of vanity's new scar tissue peeled in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly, so these letters are rearranged
peeled means the skin is removed, so tissue loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Scar tissue peeled away after a cosmetic procedure gone wrong for vanity's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peeled' strips the skin from tissue, leaving ISSU; 'in error' then shuffles that with the scar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection and wasted away.

clue.text: Rowdy Verve heading off to the States

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: brio means verve or vigour
taken as written
US stands for the United States

explanation.surface: The rowdy band Verve heading off on tour to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes the B from BRIO. The Verve are a British rock band, which makes 'Verve' look like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous behaviour is wild and disorderly, just like rowdy behaviour.

clue.text: In shots a kirsch is an exotic brew unlikely to feature on 17s

definitions.text: an exotic brew unlikely to feature on 17s

indicators.note: in means the answer is found within these words

explanation.surface: Kirsch served in shots is an unusual drink for a pub crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot sake is a Japanese rice wine served warm, unlikely on a typical English pub crawl.

clue.text: Increased pressure to overstate numbers in crime genre comeback

parts.note: to hype is to overstate

indicators.note: in means the numbers go inside the other piece
a comeback means the genre word is read backwards

parts.note: noir is a dark genre of crime fiction
tens are numbers

explanation.surface: Pressure to exaggerate figures as a crime genre makes its comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' gives RION, and 'in' puts the numbers inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertension is the medical term for high blood pressure.

clue.text: Aga alight here on 17

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish commander, who might be pictured stepping down at a pub named for a Turk

explanation.surface: A notice telling someone to get off here on route 17, with an Aga stove alight.
explanation.walkthrough: Aga looks like the kitchen stove, but it is an Ottoman title. 17 is PUB CRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turk's Head is a pub name, a place a Turkish aga might naturally stop.

clue.text: Not always fond of an upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone not always fond of a fuss or upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens intermittently happens only some of the time, never constantly.

clue.text: Back in court over fight about church leader's pilgrimage to 1 across, 2, 4 and elsewhere

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the next in this down answer
back means this piece is read in reverse

parts.note: up means in court, as in up before the judge

indicators.note: about means the fight goes around the church leader

parts.note: a brawl is a fight

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone back in court after a fight, with a church leader making a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the court word; 'over' sets it above the rest in this down answer; 'about' wraps the fight round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a tour of several pubs, here the Old Cock Inn, Dun Cow and King's Head.

clue.text: Better than average post-17 quartet?

definitions.meaning: on the golf course, a score below the standard for the round
four people under the table or the weather after a pub crawl

explanation.surface: A golfer's score or a group of four after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, scoring four strokes under the standard is very good, better than an average round.

clue.text: Alternatives to 1 across etc. for reflective sip of rose if forgoing red

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
a sip is a small part, so the answer is drawn from within these words

explanation.surface: A reflective drinker sipping rosé instead of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters OSEIFFO run inside 'rose if forgoing' and are read backwards. Offie is British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling drink to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-licences sell drink to take home, an alternative to drinking in a pub like the Old Cock Inn.

clue.text: Middle-Eastern doctor of Romney Marsh getting to grips with air pollution

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding, so the doctor's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: Doctor Syn is the smuggling clergyman hero of Russell Thorndike's novels set on Romney Marsh in Kent

indicators.note: pollution suggests the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A local doctor in Kent tackling air pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pollution' rearranges AIR to RIA, which SYN surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is in the Middle East, so its people and things are described with this adjective.

clue.text: French wines guarantee American is in a state left in charge

parts.note: AC stands for appellation contrôlée, the French wine quality guarantee

indicators.note: is in means the American piece goes inside the state

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California, a US state
US means American

explanation.surface: French wine labels guaranteeing an American is in charge in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, which is a charge laid against someone.

clue.text: Slow freight left for capital

indicators.note: for capital means put in place of the capital or first letter

parts.note: freight is cargo

explanation.surface: Slow freight trains left behind in favour of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: L replaces C, the first letter, in CARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning slow and broad.

clue.text: Half-cut fringes of sandy hair styled with grease in

indicators.note: in means the hairstyle goes inside the outer letters
fringes are the outer edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: a quiff is a hairstyle swept up with grease or gel

explanation.surface: Someone with sandy hair, fringe greased up and styled.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy; 'fringes' looks like hair but means outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy is informal British for slightly drunk, the same as half-cut.

clue.text: Magic roll I had shortly before heartless louse tucked into a brie

indicators.note: before means this piece comes first
a roll turns something over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I'd is a short form of I had

indicators.note: tucked into means one piece goes inside the other
heartless means the middle is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone eating a roll and brie, then finding a louse in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' turns ID to DI. LE, left when 'heartless' removes the middle of louse, is 'tucked into' A BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diablerie is devilry or black magic, sorcery involving devils.

clue.text: With throwaway remark devoid of depth I cover up for 17 perhaps

indicators.note: devoid of means without, so one letter is removed

parts.note: an ad lib is an improvised throwaway remark

explanation.surface: Someone making a throwaway remark to cover up where they had been.
explanation.walkthrough: AD LIB loses D ('devoid of'). The cover-up is for a pub crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an excuse that covers up where one really was.

clue.text: Little woman, born pre-Fifties

parts.note: née means born, giving NE
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A small woman born before the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Woman' suggests Louisa May Alcott's book, but this is Little Nell from Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Nell is the child heroine of Dickens's novel The Old Curiosity Shop.

clue.text: Torn older nylons not your first concern on 17

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged
not means a letter is left out of nylons
the first letter of your is picked

explanation.surface: Torn old nylon stockings are not your first concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not your first' takes Y from NYLONS. 'Torn' rearranges OLDER plus NLONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a business, and the Lord Nelson is a pub name on a pub crawl.
